title: Connected integral algebras over henselian local rings
statement: Let $R$ be a henselian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and let $S$ be a nonzero commutative $R$-algebra integral over $R$, meaning that every element of $S$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $R$. Suppose that the only idempotents of $S$ are $0$ and $1$. Then $S$ is henselian local, the structural homomorphism $R\to S$ is local, and the residue field $S/\mathfrak m_S$ is algebraic over $R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]. If $R$ is strictly henselian, then $S$ is strictly henselian as well. No finiteness, reducedness or domain hypothesis is imposed on $S$.

proof.text: Every finite R-subalgebra A of S is nonzero and inherits the zero-one idempotent condition. Apply the finite-product decomposition. Its index set is nonempty (otherwise A would be the zero ring), and a coordinate idempotent forces the index set to be subsingleton. Transport the henselian local structure from its sole factor to A.

proof.text: For s in S, the subalgebra R[s] is module-finite by integrality, hence henselian local by Step 1. Either s or 1-s is a unit in R[s], and therefore in S. The unit criterion makes S local.

source.place: Tags 04GH and 04GI; direct finite-coefficient simple-root specialization of the directed-union argument.

proof.text: An integral map of local rings contracts the target maximal ideal to a maximal ideal, which must be the unique maximal ideal of the source. It is therefore local. Apply this to R to S, and to each finite R-subalgebra A to S (integrality over A follows from the equations over R).

source.place: Tags 04GH and 04GI; direct finite-coefficient simple-root specialization of the directed-union argument.

proof.text: For a monic f over S and a0 satisfying the simple-root conditions modulo its maximal ideal, let A be the R-subalgebra generated by a0 and the finite set of coefficients of f. It is module-finite by integrality. The polynomial descends along the injective inclusion of A, and remains monic. Step 3 reflects units along A to S, hence descends both the maximal-ideal root condition and the unit derivative condition. Step 1 gives Hensel lifting in A. Map that root and its maximal-ideal congruence into S to obtain the HenselianLocalRing structure directly.

source.place: Tags 04GH and 04GI; direct finite-coefficient simple-root specialization of the directed-union argument.

proof.text: Lift any element of the residue field of S to s in S. Reduce a monic integral equation for s over R along the residue map of R. The commuting square of canonical residue maps shows that the resulting monic polynomial annihilates the chosen residue element. Monicity makes it nonzero, proving the residue extension is algebraic.

source.place: Tags 04GH and 04GI; direct finite-coefficient simple-root specialization of the directed-union argument.

proof.text: If R is strictly henselian, its residue field is separably closed. Apply Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isSepClosed, the general algebraic-extension theorem recorded by the finite-extension leaf, directly to Step 5. The residue field of S is separably closed, and Step 4 now makes S strictly henselian.
